sourcedFrom: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 (2025)
cleanIntro: The Axial is a belt-fed-rated .30 can with a 17-4 stainless body and Cobalt6 baffles, and Rugged says up front that because of how it is built it needs only LIMITED service. ⛔ What it does need is clean mounting threads. It rides a Dual Taper Lock friction mount with a locking collar and a GO gauge on the muzzle device, and the Multi-Tool lives inside the core under a finger-tight retainer.

steps.title: ⛔ Never clean it while it is on the gun
steps.action: Take the suppressor off the host before any cleaning. Rugged puts this first and states the consequence: cleaning a mounted can can lead to personal injury or death. Magazine out, chamber checked, and confirm the host is in a safe condition before you touch the muzzle device.
steps.prose: It is a solvent-and-a-loaded-chamber rule. Nothing about the can is worth working on in front of a live gun.
steps.quote: Never attempt to clean a suppressor while it’s attached to a host weapon, as this could lead to personal injury or death.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Service/Maintenance — Warning, p.1
steps.warn: Always wear proper protective equipment while performing service/maintenance. Failure to do so could result in personal injury or death.

steps.title: Collar counter-clockwise 1/2 turn — that unlocks the taper
steps.action: Let it cool first. Then turn the locking collar counter-clockwise half a rotation; that disengages the rear locking taper. The collar carries engraved LOCK / UNLOCK arrows — use them rather than guessing.
steps.prose: The Dual Taper Lock is a friction mount: two spring arms in the collar press on the muzzle device's rear taper. Half a turn releases that pressure.
steps.quote: Step 1/2 Turn the locking collar counter-clockwise a 1/2 rotation; this disengages the rear locking taper.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Removal, Step 1/2, p.4
steps.warn: Never attempt to remove a hot suppressor without the proper protective gear. Allow the suppressor to cool before removal. Failure to do so could result in personal injury or death.

steps.title: Then 2.5 turns off — by the BODY, never the collar
steps.action: With the collar disengaged, hold the Axial by its BODY and rotate the whole suppressor counter-clockwise 2.5 turns, then slide it off the muzzle device. ⛔ Do not turn it by the locking collar — that is not what the collar is for in either direction.
steps.prose: Half a turn on the collar, two and a half on the body. Two different movements on two different parts, and mixing them up is what wears a mount.
steps.quote: Step 2/2 With the rear locking collar disengaged, hold the body of the Axial and rotate the suppressor counter clockwise 2.5 turns and slide the suppressor over the muzzle device.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Removal, Step 2/2, p.4

steps.title: Mounting threads: solvent and a brush, and that is most of it
steps.action: Rugged's stated maintenance for this can is short by design — keep all the mounting threads clean and free from debris, with a small amount of gun cleaning solvent and a brush. The exotic materials in the body are why there is not more to do.
steps.prose: "Limited service/maintenance" is the maker's own phrase. Believe it and put the time into the threads instead.
steps.quote: Due to the construction and use of exotic materials, the Axial™ requires limited service/ maintenance. It is important to keep all the mounting threads clean and free from debris.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Service/Maintenance, p.1

steps.title: ⛔ ALL solvent out before use — hot soapy water, drain, compressed air
steps.action: Every trace of solvent must be off and out of the suppressor before it is fired again. Rugged's method is hot soapy water, letting the can fully drain, and compressed air — which it describes as highly recommended, not optional-feeling.
steps.prose: Solvent left inside a can is not a cleanliness problem; it is a first-round problem.
steps.quote: All solvent should be fully removed from the suppressor prior to use. This can be accomplished with hot soapy water taking care to let the suppressor fully drain before use. The use of compressed air is highly recommended.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Service/Maintenance, step 2, p.1

steps.title: ⛔ Check the BORE — before use and after every maintenance cycle
steps.action: Look through the suppressor and confirm the bore is free of debris and obstructions. Rugged makes this the operator's responsibility explicitly, and asks for it BEFORE any use AND after every maintenance cycle — twice, not once.
steps.prose: A patch, a bristle or a bead of dried solvent in the bore is a destroyed can and possibly a destroyed rifle.
steps.quote: It is the operator’s responsibility to check the bore of the suppressor to confirm that it’s free of debris/ obstructions. This should be performed before any use and after all maintenance cycles. Failure to do so could result in serious personal injury or death.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Service/Maintenance — Warning, p.1

steps.title: Collar OPEN first — clockwise until it stops
steps.action: Before the can goes anywhere near the muzzle device, open the locking collar by twisting it CLOCKWISE until it stops, using the engraved lock/unlock arrows for reference.
steps.prose: Threading on with the collar shut is how the spring arms get worked against the taper for no reason.
steps.quote: Step 1/4 Open the locking collar by twisting it clockwise until it stops. Use the engraved lock/unlock directional arrows engraved on the collar for reference.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Installation, Step 1/4, p.4

steps.title: Thread on by the BODY until fully seated
steps.action: Hold the suppressor by the main body and thread it onto the muzzle device until it is fully seated. ⛔ Not by the locking collar — Rugged says so in the step itself.
steps.prose: Same rule as removal, in reverse: body for threading, collar for locking.
steps.quote: Step 2/4 Hold the suppressor by the main body and thread suppressor onto the muzzle device until it is fully seated. Do not thread on using the locking collar.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Installation, Step 2/4, p.4

steps.title: Collar clockwise 1/2 a turn until tight
steps.action: Turn the locking collar clockwise half a turn until tight, again using the engraved arrows. That is what puts the spring arms back on the rear taper and keeps the can seated under fire.
steps.prose: Half a turn. Not tighter — the spring pressure is the design, not the torque.
steps.quote: Step 3/4 Turn the locking collar clockwise 1/2 a turn until tight. Use the engraved lock/unlock directional arrows engraved on the collar for reference.
steps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Installation, Step 3/4, p.4

deepSteps.title: The Multi-Tool lives inside the core, under a finger-tight retainer
deepSteps.action: The Multi-Tool Retainer holds the Multi-Tool inside the suppressor core and gives the can a surface to rest on in a vice. It is FINGER TIGHT and that is all it needs — the finger grooves are there so it comes in and out quickly. ⛔ Rugged says do not use the Multi-Tool without the retainer.
deepSteps.prose: This is the part people lose. It is not a fastener; it is a holder and a vice pad.
deepSteps.caution: Do not use the Multi-Tool without the retainer.
deepSteps.quote: The retainer is installed finger tight which is all that is required to perform it’s function.
deepSteps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Components and Tools — Multi-Tool Retainer, p.3

deepSteps.title: The R.U.M. mount is torqued to 25 ft-lb and needs a vice
deepSteps.action: The Axial ships with the Rugged Universal Mount pre-installed to 25 foot-pounds. To take it off or put it back at the right torque, Rugged recommends a bench vice on the SUPPRESSOR side and a torque wrench with a socket on the MOUNT side. ⚠ The two flats on the outer ring are for unlocking a collar that has come loose on the gun — Rugged does NOT recommend using them to install or remove the mount.
deepSteps.prose: There is a right tool for this joint and a wrong one that is right there on the same part.
deepSteps.aside: We do NOT recommend using the flats to install or remove the mount from the suppressor.
deepSteps.quote: Axial comes with the R.U.M. pre-installed to torque specification (25 ft-lb).
deepSteps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Components and Tools — Rugged Universal Mount, p.3

deepSteps.title: Anti-seize on the universal thread — every time it comes apart
deepSteps.action: The 1.375x24 universal thread is lightly coated with anti-seize from the factory to stop galling and seizing. Any time the mount comes off and goes back on, clean the threads of debris and make sure anti-seize is present again. ⚠ Rugged notes the thread fits other makers' mounts but recommends its own products.
deepSteps.prose: Stainless on stainless galls. That coating is not decoration.
deepSteps.quote: To prevent galling and seizing, the suppressor’s universal thread is lightly coated with anti-seize. Ensure any time the mount is removed and re-installed, that the threads are clean of debris and anti-seize is present to prevent unnecessary issues.
deepSteps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Installation, p.4

deepSteps.title: Front cap threads take white lithium grease
deepSteps.action: The interior front cap threads ship coated with white lithium grease. Rugged recommends adding more to the front cap threads through the life of the can as needed. The flash hider front cap is stainless and every other Rugged rifle front cap fits the Axial.
deepSteps.prose: A cap that is only ever run dry is a cap that eventually will not come off.
deepSteps.quote: It is recommended to apply additional white lithium grease to the front cap threads throughout use as needed.
deepSteps.cite: AXIAL — BELT-FED RATED 7.62 SUPPRESSOR OPERATOR’S MANUAL — REV-06-23-25 — Axial Installation, p.4

cleaning.name: MOUNTING THREADS — THE STATED JOB
tasks: Small amount of gun cleaning solvent and a brush
Threads left clean and free of debris
Anti-seize present on the 1.375x24 universal thread whenever the mount returns

cleaning.name: SOLVENT REMOVAL
tasks: Compressed air — Rugged calls it highly recommended

cleaning.name: BORE CHECK — TWICE
tasks: Free of debris and obstructions, confirmed by looking

cleaning.name: MOUNT AND CAP
tasks: R.U.M. at 25 ft-lb, vice on the suppressor side, torque wrench on the mount
White lithium grease on the front cap threads as needed
Multi-Tool stored in the core under its finger-tight retainer

reassembly: Locking collar OPEN — clockwise until it stops.
Thread on by the BODY until fully seated. Never by the collar.
Locking collar clockwise 1/2 turn until tight.
GO gauge checked: only "GO" visible at the collar.
Bore confirmed clear before the host is loaded.
fncheck: ⛔ Read the GO gauge. On the wrench flat of the Dual Taper Lock muzzle device is a go gauge; using the bottom of the lock collar as the visual guide, a correctly mounted Axial shows only "GO". If you can see NO-GO, it is not properly mounted and does not get fired. Then confirm the bore is clear of debris and obstructions — Rugged makes that the operator's responsibility before any use — and that the host's threads are concentric to the bore, checked by a gunsmith if you are unsure.
